Carine Zheng · Website design directions · updated 23 Nov 2026

Six looks for one page.

Design previews for Carine to react to. Design 07 is new: design 06 with her four planning areas told inside one painting that changes as you scroll. Design 06 is the hand-painted watercolour look told as an album of memories still to be made. Her four planning areas are written on the backs of the photographs, and the visitor ends by choosing the pages they are working towards. Design 05 is the same look told as a story of what she does, and design 04 is the same look as a simple page. The first three each follow a Webflow template. All six use the same approved words and the same portrait; design 06 also adds a new headline and short captions, which are drafts for Carine and her compliance team to approve. Best viewed on a laptop; each also works on a phone. For comparison, the current draft is here (opens in a new tab).

07The living picture

New · scroll to play

Design 06 with its middle rebuilt as one picture. The cottage painting stays on screen and her four areas happen inside it across one day: a storm and an umbrella, a sapling that grows, four arrivals for marriage, a home, children and other major changes, then golden hour. Each ends with a shutter click and a print for the album. Open design →

06Album

scroll to play

The watercolour look, told as an album that is not finished yet. Empty frames fill with paint as you scroll; four prints turn over to show the planning behind them, in Carine’s own words; the rain, the growing plant and golden hour follow; and at the end you choose the pages you are working towards and send them to her on WhatsApp. Open design →

05Story

scroll to play

The watercolour look, told as you scroll. One polaroid frame shows life changing; a lens clears a muddled painting; rain falls until the umbrella opens; a seedling grows into a full-grown plant; the steps arrive as a conversation; night falls on “Let’s talk”, where a note goes straight to WhatsApp. Open design →

04Watercolour

simple page

Simple and hand-painted. Cream paper, soft watercolour washes and little painted stickers, with Carine’s portrait as a taped polaroid. Her four planning areas become a hand-drawn route through life’s stages, and the three steps are notes taped down and stamped. Open design →

01Editorial

after SaleUnion

Crisp and confident. A big serif headline, small typewriter-style labels, and soft mint and pink panels that keep a professional page from feeling stiff. Closes on a dark call to action. Open design →

02Cinematic

after Fernvale

Bold and modern. Opens on a full-screen dark scene built around the portrait, then quiet white sections, one big quote in Carine’s own words and a dark contact panel. Open design →

03Bento

after Astrixo

Warm and orderly. Everything sits in rounded cream tiles with an elegant condensed serif, a little like a well-kept desk. Closest in mood to the current beige trial. Open design →

The same in all six

  • Rebecca’s v1 copy, word for word: the four planning areas, the three steps and the contact section. Design 05 adds only short labels and the note field. Design 06 adds a headline, short captions and the page chooser, all listed as drafts in STORYBOARD-06.md.
  • One call to action, WhatsApp, with the floating button on every scroll position.
  • The regulatory details and the footer disclaimer, which is still placeholder wording until Financial Alliance compliance signs off.
  • No testimonials, client numbers or stock photos. Where a template relies on those, the slot holds a real detail or an honest “photo to come”.
Mock-ups only: the video tiles and most social links are placeholders, and nothing here is live or indexed by search engines.
